scope: Two-node LXD Kubernetes 1.37.0 cluster on A1. No live-cluster upgrade and no connection to production PostgreSQL, Kafka, credentials, or application data.

Cross-node Pod IP, ClusterIP Service, and CoreDNS resolution passed
Default-deny NetworkPolicy blocked traffic and selected allow restored it

Observed Git revision 8088f4c0d970abb09e250248cc97e35623447cb5
Controller, cainjector, and webhook became Ready

A valid 1h1m Certificate was issued and naturally renewed from revision 1 to 2

Persistent broker restart changed UID ba008341-a954-4752-9363-3404273bb52f to 9f1cc622-488c-4b37-ba89-bf66f73e14eb while retaining message k137-persistent-1-1789986349 and ACLs

evidence: Official schema hooks created default and visibility schemas and namespace k137-test
Cluster health returned SERVING
Workflow k137-persistence-1789988053 started with run 01a0c39a-247d-7591-949e-29983360e579 and history length 2
Restarting frontend, history, matching, and worker changed all four Pod UIDs while preserving the same workflow and history
Restarting PostgreSQL changed UID 6f2c7c4f-599c-498f-b1a1-88437c9657fe to ac21fbb0-9e48-425a-a9c1-b1e5fa607d06; Temporal returned SERVING and the same workflow history remained readable

limits: The worker memory limit was raised from 1500 MiB to 2500 MiB after runtime components showed resource pressure; this is a recorded test-environment correction, not a production sizing result.
This is a two-node compatibility environment with one control plane and one worker; it does not prove three-control-plane or three-broker host-failure high availability.
Small isolated payloads validate APIs and behavior, not production throughput, capacity, or six-node disk contention.
Several upstream support matrices still stop before Kubernetes 1.37; these results are project evidence, not a vendor support statement.
Live migration still requires fresh backups, restore evidence, sequential Kubernetes minor upgrades, and per-step rollback gates.
